title: Expo and Defense
outcome: By the end, I can defend a project using measured results, limits and an honest baseline comparison.
scenario: A fictional paper sorter team prepares an exhibition evidence board.
given: Both prototype and manual baseline attempt the same 10 reserved cases. Prototype passes 8; baseline passes 9.
Two additional planned cases are unrun. No timing or pupil-satisfaction measures were collected.

steps.label: Describe contract
steps.detail: Show the task, inputs, rule and reserved case selection.

steps.label: Keep incomplete work
steps.detail: Two unrun cases remain visible, without pass/fail labels.

steps.label: Defend conclusion
steps.detail: Prototype did not beat baseline on this measured outcome; explain its failures.

explanation: An exhibition should make the evidence inspectable. A polished demonstration is not a substitute for the reserved-case record. The shared cases allow a direct descriptive comparison of pass rates; missing timing data prevents a claim that the prototype is faster. Unrun cases must not be treated as successes.

counterfactual.change: Someone adds the two unrun cases to the denominator as failures.
counterfactual.prediction: That reports a different measure, 8/12 completed successes out of planned cases.
counterfactual.reason: It cannot be called the original attempted-case pass rate; distinguish completion from evaluated correctness.

student_task: Write one defensible success statement and one claim the evidence cannot support.
teacher_answer: Defensible: 8 of 10 attempted reserved cases passed. Unsupported: the prototype is faster or more accurate than the baseline.
project_evidence: Present the Helpful Classroom Sorter’s versions, test records, baseline, failures and next investigation as an evidence portfolio.
limits: This fictional evaluation does not demonstrate classroom learning impact or performance on every future request.
review_note: Individually reviewed fictional topic example; arithmetic and declared policies checked. This is supported practice, not the reserved independent assessment.
